description: Committee recommends replacing infill drainage plans with commitment letters.
This aims to simplify permits and reduce developer costs.
Public speakers raised concerns about reduced oversight and neighbor impacts.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
6 for, 0 against
Committee requested options for a cost recovery model for drainage enforcement.
Mayor Block stated making it harder for existing residents is not okay.
Residents in Nutana, Varsity View, Buena Vista, Queen Elizabeth, Exhibition, Hall of Tain.
Lack of community consultation on proposed changes was questioned.
Nutana Community Association opposed the proposed bylaw amendments.
Administration will focus on groundwater mitigation in the coming year.

speakers.name: Margaret Thompson
speakers.summary: Margaret Thompson spoke in opposition to the proposed amendments expressing concerns that the changes could reduce oversight of drainage requirements for infill developments, potentially resulting in drainage issues and additional impact...
said: Current bylaw successfully reduced infill complaints; weakening it is concerning.
New process shifts burden to inexperienced owners, delaying problem detection.
Proposed changes increase costs, allow unscrupulous builders, harm neighbors.

speakers.name: Robert Clipperton
speakers.summary: Robert Clipperton spoke in opposition to the proposed amendments expressing concerns regarding the potential impacts of the proposed changes on drainage oversight for infill developments, neighbouring properties, and community consultati...
said: Current bylaw effectively reduced drainage complaints; relaxing requirements is unwise.
No community consultation occurred regarding these significant proposed changes.
New process shifts burden to neighbors, creates enforcement issues.

segments.title: Staff Presentation on Drainage Bylaw Amendments
segments.takeaway: Administration presented proposed amendments to the drainage bylaw, aiming to simplify the building permit process and reduce costs by replacing site-grading plans with a letter of commitment.

segments.title: Public Comment: Margaret Thompson
segments.takeaway: Resident Margaret Thompson opposed the bylaw amendments, citing personal drainage issues from infill development and concerns about delayed problem detection and lack of accountability.

segments.title: Public Comment: Robert Clipper-Din
segments.takeaway: Robert Clipper-Din, representing the Nutana Community Association, urged rejection of the proposal, arguing the current bylaw is effective and community consultation was lacking.

segments.title: Committee Discussion and Questions to Administration
segments.takeaway: Committee members questioned administration about the proposed changes, focusing on housing affordability, cost recovery models, and the effectiveness of current and proposed enforcement mechanisms.

segments.title: Motion for Cost Recovery Model
segments.takeaway: The committee passed a motion directing administration to report back on options for a cost recovery model to fund drainage enforcement for infill development.

description: City will temporarily remove 25 downtown benches and evaluate public amenities.
Further bench removals are deferred until September 2027.
City will explore a dedicated reporting line for businesses.

chips.text: Approved
6 for, 0 against
Pilot project costs about $30,000, funded by BID streetscape reserve.
Administration noted removing benches often displaces social disorder, not solves it.
Downtown businesses and commercial property owners will use new reporting line.
Pilot project will inform future decisions on public amenities across BIDs.
Peer-reviewed research on bench removal impact on social disorder was not provided.
Downtown BID strongly supported the temporary bench management pilot project.
Concerns raised about equity and accessibility for bus riders and people needing rest.
Administration committed to monitoring conditions and collecting data during the pilot.

speakers.name: Sara Wheelwright
speakers.summary: Sara Wheelwright, on behalf of the Downtown Saskatoon Business Improvement District, spoke in support of the proposed bench management and maintenance pilot project.
said: Benches are chronic hotspots for public disorder, sanitation, and safety concerns.
25 benches are unsafe, unsanitary, and beyond small maintenance interventions.
Pilot project is data-driven to fix broken benches for a welcoming downtown.

segments.title: Administration presents bench removal request report
segments.takeaway: Administration presented a report outlining the downtown business improvement district's request to remove benches and enhance maintenance, proposing a temporary operational trial.

segments.title: Downtown BID presents case for bench removal pilot
segments.takeaway: The Downtown BID chair advocated for the temporary bench removal pilot project, citing public disorder, sanitation, and safety concerns at specific bench locations.

segments.title: Questions for Downtown BID speaker
segments.takeaway: Councillors questioned the BID speaker on the evidence for bench removal, the impact on accessibility, and the effectiveness of existing downtown support resources.

segments.title: Questions for administration on bench removal report
segments.takeaway: Councillors asked administration about enhanced maintenance, structural integrity of benches, data collection, and the effectiveness of bench removal in addressing social disorder.

segments.title: Councillor Parker's motion on bench management
segments.takeaway: Councillor Parker moved to defer further bench removals, undertake a comprehensive evaluation of public amenities, and engage with the BID on maintenance roles and funding.

segments.title: Amendment to Councillor Parker's motion
segments.takeaway: Councillor Keller proposed an amendment to include potential involvement of social entrepreneur organizations for cleaning within the BID area in the motion.

segments.title: Mayor Block's motion for dedicated reporting line
segments.takeaway: Mayor Block moved for administration to report on the feasibility of implementing a dedicated reporting option for businesses and commercial property owners to report concerns.

segments.title: Committee comments before vote
segments.takeaway: Committee members shared final comments on the motions, emphasizing the need for accountability and efficiency in addressing downtown issues.

segments.title: Committee votes on motions
segments.takeaway: The committee voted to approve all five motions, including deferring bench removals, evaluating amenities, engaging the BID, and exploring a dedicated reporting line.
